verdict.rationale: Link CLI documents per-purchase consent: the agent creates a spend request for a specific purchase, the customer approves it on the Link website or mobile app, and only then does Link return a one-time-use credential. Shared payment tokens act as a scoped mandate with currency, max amount and expiration limits plus revocation, and the Stripe MCP server requires human approval, expiring after 24 hours, before outbound payments and refunds. Missing for 10: a documented human-approval step on the MPP/x402 machine-payments rail (a community post notes MPP covers 'how agents pay' but not 'did anyone authorize this'), an explicit buyer-consent step in ACS embedded checkout, and independent hands-on corroboration of the approval flows.
